transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I just need someone to finally listen to me. For months now, I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

It's happening all the time, and I see the signs. Like, I work as a billing clerk, and these little billing errors will just show up out of nowhere. Or someone at church will suddenly act real funny toward me, like they've been told something about me. People keep telling me I'm wrong, but no matter what records anyone pulls up to try and explain it away, I know it all ties back to them.
Do you believe your husband’s family has any special way of controlling events or sending messages that other people wouldn’t normally be able to do?

No, I don't... I mean, I'm not saying they have superpowers or anything like that. I'm not sure what you mean by special. 

They just do things the regular way. You know, making phone calls, whispering to people behind my back, maybe logging into the system at my job to mess up the paperwork. It's just... they're very sneaky and organized about it. But no, they don't have any kind of magic or special powers to control things, if that's what you're asking. They're just using normal, everyday ways to ruin my life.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

No, I don't hear voices. Nothing like that. I mean, I hear real people when they're whispering or talking about me, but... no, I'm not hearing things in my head when no one is around, if that's what you mean. I don't hear things that aren't there.
Before all this started, had you been diagnosed with any brain illness or injury?
No, I haven't. I've never had a head injury or... any kind of brain illness. My health has always been perfectly fine. I've never had any problems like that before all this started.
Did all of this start very suddenly?

No, it wasn't sudden. It's been going on for about nine months now. It all started back then, right around the time my husband's family and I had a big falling out over some money issues and... well, what they expected for the holidays. That's when all of this really began.
Do you believe your husband's family can do things to you that would be impossible in real life?

No, I don't think that. I mean, they aren't doing magic or anything... impossible. They're just regular people. They're just doing normal, sneaky things to mess with my life. I know they don't have superpowers or anything like that, if that's what you're asking.
Aside from this problem with your husband’s family, has your day-to-day functioning gotten much worse?

No, not really. I still get up for work every day. I do my job as a billing clerk just fine, and I keep the house running. I even still have time for my hobbies, like gardening and a bit of painting. My life is mostly normal. The only real issue is when I try to explain to people what my in-laws are doing to me. That's when things get difficult, because people don't always want to listen. But other than that, no, I'm functioning just fine.
Have you noticed yourself becoming much less interested in socializing or in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I still like doing the things I've always done, like my gardening and painting. And I still talk to my friends and coworkers. I haven't lost interest in any of that. It's just... well, like I said, it gets frustrating when I try to talk about what his family is up to and people look at me funny. But I still want to be around people and do my hobbies. None of that has changed.
Has anyone told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way they can’t understand?

No, nobody has ever said anything like that to me. I think I speak pretty clearly. I mean, I have to talk to people all day at work, and they understand me just fine. I stay on topic. The only time people get confused is when they don't want to believe what I'm telling them about my in-laws, but that's not because I'm not making sense. It's just because they don't want to hear it. So, no, I don't jump around or talk in a way people can't follow.
Have you had a marked decrease in your emotional expression, like your face or voice seeming much less expressive than usual?

No, I don't think so. Nobody has mentioned anything like that to me. I mean, I still laugh at jokes at work, and I definitely show it when I'm upset or frustrated about... well, everything going on with his family. I'm pretty expressive, I'd say. So, no, my face and my voice are just the same as they've always been.
